newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Malaysia's Mahathir calls for global commonwealth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir calls for global commonwealth.

text.p: Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday called for a single global commonwealth for the next millennium, in which nations work together for mutual prosperity.
Speaking at a European Research Centre conference for business and investment, Mahathir called for a global effort to ensure that no single nation or region dominates the future.
"All nations, all people, all regions should have opportunity. I hope that all people of talent and diligence, who earn the right, will inherit the future," he said.
A "world century" was now possible for the first time, as opposed to eras dominated by Europe and the United States.
"The constraints have removed themselves. We must make it (a world century) our mission in the new millennium," he told delegates.
Mahathir argued against a new hegemony of Asian nations.
"The damnation that is domination will be no lesser if it is Asian domination."
He said, despite theories to the contrary, East Asian nations could continue their strong economic growth without a similar growth of aggression.

"I believe we will not fight. We will patiently build the East Asian peace, the East Asian community, the web of East Asian cooperation which we must have in order to ensure that we can continue with our rapid march towards a better life for our peoples," said Mahathir.
He added that each nation would first need to adjust their mindsets, but would eventually blossom by cooperating with the global commonwealth.
"Imagine the incredible results if the whole world is in the grips not of 'beggar-thy-neighbour' impulses but is given the push of 'prosper-thy-neighbour' attitudes and policies," Mahathir said.
"If this is unrealistic idealism? Come to our region to see how unrealistic we are."
